बॉस! सनी देओल के ओटीटी डेब्यू को लेकर सामने आया है बड़ा और चटपटा किस्सा! 🎬✨

Netflix की Ruchikaa Kapoor Sheikh ने Hindustan Times को दिए इंटरव्यू में बताया कि 40 साल से थिएटर्स में तहलका मचाने वाले Sunny Deol अपने ओटीटी डेब्यू को लेकर घबराए हुए थे। 🤩

Ruchikaa Kapoor Sheikh का दावा है कि Sunny Deol इस बात से परेशान थे कि Netflix की लीगल ड्रामा फिल्म Ikka में कोई एक्शन सीन नहीं है, जबकि पिछले चार दशकों से एक्शन उनकी पहचान रहा है। 🧐

report के mutabik, जब Ruchikaa ने उन्हें Netflix पर डेब्यू करने के लिए कहा, तो 60 साल के Sunny Deol हंसते हुए बोले थे— "मैं 60 साल का हूं, मेरा डेब्यू कैसे हो सकता है?" 😅

Sunny Deol ने यह भी कहा था कि Border 2 हाल ही में आई है, तो क्या आप वाकई शोर हैं? हालांकि बाद में उन्होंने टीम के भरोसे पर हामी भर दी और कहा कि वह अपना सौ प्रतिशत देंगे। 🙌

तो क्या आप भी सनी पाजी को बिना एक्शन के इस अलग अंदाज़ में देखना पसंद करते हैं? नीचे कमेंट करके जल्दी से बताओ! 👇

ctx.title: Sunny Deol was apprehensive about OTT 'debut' with a non-action film like Ikka right after Border 2, recalls Netflix's Ruchikaa Kapoor Sheikh
ctx.summary: After over 40 years of giving theatrical hits, Sunny Deol moved to streaming with Siddharth P Malhotra's courtroom drama, Ikka, which released on Netflix.
ctx.text:
After more than 40 years of giving theatrical hits, Sunny Deol surprised one and all with his streaming debut in 2026. The actor starred in Netflix ’s Ikka, directed by Siddharth P Malhotra. The legal drama, which also starred Akshaye Khanna, was a success on the platform, reaching the number one spot in its first few days.
Ruchikaa Kapoor Sheikh, Director, Original Films, Netflix India, takes Hindustan Times behind the scenes of how the streamer convinced the superstar to opt for a streaming film and how he let go of his action-hero image for the courtroom drama.
Ruchikaa recalls that Sunny was initially apprehensive about the film because it had no action, which has been his USP for close to four decades. “We were working on Ikka with Sunny sir, and he was worried that there was no action. And I told him, ‘That's the beauty of doing streaming. We'll take a familiar genre like a courtroom drama, put you in the genre, and we're going to see where it goes.’
Ruchikaa says the actor was still apprehensive when she assured him, saying, “Two months later, either I'll tell you, we should have put one action scene, or you'll call me and say this was not a bad idea. So, let's see where it goes,” she says.
She adds that she felt the freshness and novelty of the idea was what appealed to the audience. “I'm not going to blow your mind after the hand pump (scene from Gadar). We have Border and Jaat on our service. People are watching that. But if I'm going to look at original films to be able to stand on their own two feet, it has to be a complementary offering: getting someone you love in a genre that you like to click and stay on.”
Ikka happened to be Sunny’s streaming debut. Having been a theatrical star for four decades, it was a brave move for the actor. Ruchikaa recalls telling Sunny several times that it was time for him to ‘debut’ on Netflix. To which the star laughed and said, “I'm 60 years old. How can I debut?”
Ikka, Ruchikaa admits, was an unusual streaming debut for the actor who has seen a second wind to his career on the back of action extravaganzas like Gadar 2, Border 2, and Jaat. “He said, ‘Are you sure? Border abhi aayi hai (Border 2 has just released).’” But eventually he came around, Ruchikaa recalls. "I'm going with the conviction that you guys have, and I'm going to give you my all," is what he told the team.
But Ruchikaa maintains that the film's makers, including those at Netflix, were never unsure about it. “I don't want to say we were nervous. It was him and his A game, him and his element,” she explains.
Abhimanyu Mathur is Deputy Editor, Entertainment at Hindustan Times. With almost 15 years of experience in writing about everything from films and TV shows to cricket matches and elections, he inhales and exhales pop culture and news. Currently, he watches movies and TV shows and talks to celebrities for a living, while occasionally writing about them as well.

A journalism graduate of Delhi College of Arts and Commerce, Delhi University, Abhimanyu began his career with Hindustan Times at the age of 20, swapping classrooms for newsrooms at an early age. He began his journey in the early days of digital journalism, later switching to the madness of print journalism.

Work has led him to far off places like Japan and Jordan, as well as to the interiors of Haryana and the Indo-Pak border. He dabbled in city reporting in places like Meerut, Gurgaon, and Delhi, covered the Olympics and Cricket World Cups, before finding his calling in entertainment and lifestyle during the pandemic. A Rotten Tomatoes Certified Film Critic, he is equally at home covering stories on ground as he is interviewing celebrities and studios, and sometimes prefers to shepherd teams in delivering traffic through the day.
